clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is starting formal algebra — using letters to stand for unknown numbers, turning word descriptions into expressions, spotting when two expressions are equivalent, and thinking of an equation as a balance.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is getting more fluent with algebra — expanding brackets that involve negative numbers, substituting negative values into expressions, rewriting expressions to show what they mean, and solving word problems with linear equations.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is extending their number sense into algebra — using the laws of exponents, including zero and negative powers, working with square and cube roots and scientific notation, and seeing why a straight line has a constant slope.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is building core algebra skills — solving and rearranging equations, writing equations of lines, solving pairs of simultaneous equations, multiplying and factorising polynomials, and solving simple quadratics.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is deepening their algebra — completing the square and using the quadratic formula, simplifying surds and algebraic fractions, graphing inequalities, and working with fractional exponents and exponential graphs.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is tackling advanced algebra — dividing polynomials, solving quadratic inequalities and rational equations, splitting fractions into partial fractions, summing arithmetic and geometric series, and expanding brackets with the binomial theorem.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to prove results about series — using proof by induction, summing series by the method of differences, seeing why the harmonic series grows without limit, and expanding brackets raised to fractional or negative powers.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is beginning calculus — understanding the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change, differentiating to find gradients, tangents and turning points, solving optimisation problems, and integrating to find areas and accumulated change.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is mastering calculus techniques — the chain, product and quotient rules, integration by substitution and by parts, differential equations, Maclaurin series, and calculus with parametric, polar and hyperbolic functions.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning what statistics is for — asking questions that have variable answers, sorting data into types, drawing dot plots and histograms, and measuring spread with the mean absolute deviation.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to summarise data — finding averages from frequency tables, choosing the most suitable average when there are outliers, and understanding the difference between a population and a sample.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to collect and summarise data well — using quartiles, box plots and two-way tables, choosing random samples and spotting bias, and recognising misleading graphs and statistics.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to compare sets of data — using box plots and cumulative frequency graphs, describing the shape of a distribution, and understanding why results vary from one sample to another.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to measure and question data — calculating standard deviation, spotting outliers, reading histograms with unequal bars, interpreting correlation, and telling surveys, experiments and observational studies apart.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how statisticians draw conclusions — fitting regression lines, using the normal distribution, and following the logic of a hypothesis test with hypotheses, significance levels, p-values and critical regions.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning advanced statistical testing — t-tests and confidence intervals, chi-squared tests, tests for correlation and for Poisson rates, the risk of wrong conclusions, and how to choose the right test for the data.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is meeting the idea of a function — a rule giving exactly one output for each input — comparing functions shown as tables, graphs and equations, and telling linear from nonlinear relationships.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to describe and use functions — writing function notation, finding domain and range, reading key features of graphs, calculating average rates of change, and building linear models from real situations.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to model the world with functions — comparing linear and exponential growth, modelling growth and decay, finding inverse and composite functions, transforming graphs, and following the full modelling cycle.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to test models against data — using logarithms to undo exponentials, straightening curved data to test a relationship, judging fits with residuals, and modelling with quadratic functions.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is exploring new families of functions — describing curves and motion with parametric equations, and learning the hyperbolic functions sinh, cosh and tanh, their identities and inverses, and the hanging-chain curve.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to explain their geometry — solving angle problems and giving a clear reason, such as angles on a straight line or in a triangle, for every step.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning more geometry vocabulary and measurement — using bearings to describe direction, naming the parts of a circle such as chords, arcs and tangents, and finding the surface area of prisms and cylinders.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to reason and prove in geometry — using precise definitions, proving facts about angles and Pythagoras' theorem, combining transformations, working with similar shapes, and starting trigonometry.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is building a full toolkit for shapes and triangles — proving congruence and similarity, using the sine and cosine rules and exact trig values, applying circle theorems, and writing the equation of a circle.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is extending geometry into new systems — measuring angles in radians, solving trigonometric equations, proving circle theorems, using vectors in three dimensions, and meeting polar coordinates and conic sections.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is studying advanced geometry — equations of lines and planes in 3-D with dot and cross products, double-angle formulae, sketching curves in polar coordinates, and the properties of ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is meeting two new kinds of mathematical object — matrices, used to transform shapes and solve systems of equations, and complex numbers, which extend the number line so that every quadratic has solutions.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is exploring matrices and complex numbers in depth — eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalisation, Markov chains, de Moivre's theorem, roots of complex numbers, and loci drawn in the Argand diagram.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is using probability to make predictions — working out how often an outcome is expected in many trials and designing simulations to estimate probabilities.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning rules for combining probabilities — adding probabilities of events that cannot happen together, and counting outcomes by multiplying the number of choices at each step.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how events combine — multiplying probabilities for independent events and describing events as sets of outcomes within a sample space.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is working with linked events — using the general addition rule, tree diagrams for events that affect each other, and conditional probability from tables and Venn diagrams.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about probability models — conditional probability, permutations and combinations, expected value, and the binomial and Poisson distributions for counting successes and random events.

clusters.subject: Mathematics
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to combine and choose probability models — adding random variables, approximating one distribution with another, using the geometric distribution, and judging which model fits a situation.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is beginning to study electricity in more depth — explaining static charge as electrons moving between objects, and measuring current and voltage with ammeters and voltmeters.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the conventions of circuits and magnets — the difference between conventional current and electron flow, standard symbols for circuit components, and how permanent and induced magnets differ.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how circuits work quantitatively — current as flow of charge, voltage as energy per charge, how components such as diodes and thermistors behave, and how homes are wired safely.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how electricity and magnetism work together — solving multi-step circuit problems and explaining how motors, loudspeakers, generators, transformers and the National Grid work.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is studying advanced electricity — resistivity, Kirchhoff's laws, potential dividers, internal resistance, capacitors, the laws of electromagnetic induction, and how the grid keeps supply matched to demand.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how energy is stored and moves — tracing energy transfer pathways, seeing how kinetic energy depends on mass and speed and how stored energy grows with height, and telling temperature apart from thermal energy.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how heat moves — defining a system, explaining conduction, convection and infrared radiation, measuring specific heat capacity, and understanding why dissipated energy is less useful.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to calculate with energy — working out kinetic and gravitational potential energy, reducing wasted energy, reading energy bills in kilowatt-hours, and understanding thermal equilibrium.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to apply energy conservation — calculating elastic, electrical and stored energy, explaining how power stations generate electricity, and comparing energy resources using data.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is linking energy to work and heat flow — using the work–energy principle, calculating temperatures when substances mix, explaining why heat flows from hot to cold, and building energy-accounting models.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to analyse forces — telling scalars from vectors, drawing free-body diagrams, finding the overall force on an object, and understanding inertia.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to describe and predict motion — using velocity, acceleration and velocity–time graphs, applying F = ma, and working with momentum, springs, liquid pressure and stopping distances.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the laws of motion in depth — using the equations of motion, explaining terminal velocity and friction, conserving momentum in collisions, resolving vectors, and describing fields.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is studying advanced mechanics — collisions, forces on slopes, projectile and circular motion, and the inverse-square laws for gravitational and electric forces.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is using the particle model to explain diffusion — how particles move and spread out from where they are concentrated.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is using the particle model to explain everyday observations — temperature, gas pressure, melting and evaporation — and learning about atoms, density, and how chemical reactions rearrange atoms.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the structure of atoms and how reactions are written — atomic and mass numbers, how the atomic model developed, balancing chemical equations, and what happens to mass in a reaction.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how electrons explain chemistry — the periodic table, ionic and covalent bonding, chemical formulae, collision theory, and the hydrocarbons in crude oil and how they are separated and used.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning quantitative and organic chemistry — the mole and reacting masses, bonding and structure, rates and energy changes, radioactivity, and families of organic compounds such as alcohols, acids and polymers.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is studying advanced chemistry — equilibrium, redox and nuclear reactions, organic reaction mechanisms, orbitals and bonding, the structure of benzene, and identifying compounds with mass spectrometry and infrared.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is studying advanced organic chemistry — reactions of benzene and carbonyl compounds, NMR spectroscopy, planning multi-step syntheses, optical isomers, and the chemistry of amino acids, proteins and chromatography.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning what waves are — understanding that waves carry energy without carrying matter, linking amplitude to energy, and reading wave diagrams and graphs.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to describe waves with numbers — frequency, period and wave speed — and exploring sound waves, hearing range and ultrasound, reflection, and analog and digital signals.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how waves behave — measuring the speed of sound, using echoes, explaining refraction and lenses, and exploring the properties and uses of the electromagnetic spectrum.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about wave effects and technologies — interference, diffraction, resonance, optical fibres, the eye and cameras, ultrasound imaging, radiation risks, and storing and sending information digitally.

clusters.subject: Science
clusters.summary: Your child is studying advanced wave physics — standing waves, Snell's law and the lens equation, polarisation, photons and the wave–particle nature of light, the Doppler effect, and red-shift in an expanding universe.
